correctness.rationale: For connected noncomplete strongly regular G, the defining identity A²=(k-mu)I+(lambda-mu)A+mu J and k(k-lambda-1)=(v-k-1)mu yield the stated resolvent (zI+L)^-1=[(z+b)I+A+(mu/z)J]/[z²+pz+v mu] for z>0. Jacobi complementary minor identity converts det(zI+L_FF) for any three-leader S to the global determinant times the 3x3 resolvent minor. Separating its universal logarithmic derivative K_G and computing det(rI+A_S), 1^Tadj(rI+A_S)1 for the four induced 3-vertex graphs gives all Phi_e(b,mu). Since connected noncomplete SRG has b>=3 and mu>=1, the three exact consecutive Phi gaps have strictly positive factored numerators and denominators. Therefore each C(S) strictly increases with induced leader-edge count. In the complement, degree d=v-k-1 and adjacent common-neighbor number t=v-2k+mu-2 imply that the first existing pattern is a triangle (t>0), a length-2 path (t=0,d>=2), or matching edge (d=1), yielding respective complete optimal counts vdt/6, vd(d-1)/2, and v(v-2)/2. All classifications use only actual graph triples and do not assume SRG vertex-transitivity.
